title: Finite pushforward preserves punctual upper bounds and purity
statement:
Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a finite morphism of separated finite-type schemes over a finite field, and let $\mathcal G$ be a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf on $X_0$. If every local Frobenius eigenvalue of $\mathcal G$ at every closed point has weight at most $w$, then the same holds for $f_{0*}\mathcal G$. If $\mathcal G$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$, then $f_{0*}\mathcal G$ is punctually $\iota$-pure of weight $w$.
Here finite morphism, constructibility, Weil sheaves, and direct image use [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-constructible-heart], [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and [def-weil-derived-direct-image], with weights as in [def-weil-punctual-weights].

source.place: general finite-pushforward proof: exactness and finite-stalk Frobenius-cycle argument (paragraph beginning “A finite morphism is proper” through the displayed absolute-value calculation)

proof.text: Base change the finite morphism to the fixed algebraic closure of the finite field. The rational finite-direct-image statement [lem-zl-finite-adic-direct-image] applies to this base change: the direct image of a constructible Qbar sheaf is in the constructible heart, the finite direct-image functor is exact, and for every geometric point y the stalk is naturally the direct sum of the stalks over the finite geometric fibre. Its naturality for semilinear automorphisms identifies the Weil/Frobenius operator on the direct-image stalk with the operator that permutes the fibre stalks.

source.place: Finite stalk formula and Frobenius cycles, with relative residue degree and point transport made explicit

proof.text: Fix a closed point y of Y_0 and view the finite fibre over Spec kappa(y) as a finite scheme over that finite field. Apply [lem-a1-finite-weil-sections-decomposition] to the restriction of G to this fibre. Under the stalk identification of Step 1, the fibre decomposition is a direct sum of Frobenius-stable cyclic blocks. If x is a closed point of the fibre and e=[kappa(x):kappa(y)], the geometric Frobenius at y cyclically permutes the e stalk summands and its e-th power on each summand is the local Frobenius F_x. The same statement records that the geometric points in the block are exactly the lifts of x, so no reducedness or etaleness hypothesis is being added.

source.place: Finite stalk formula and Frobenius cycles, with relative residue degree and point transport made explicit

proof.text: Let μ be an eigenvalue of the direct-image Frobenius on a nonzero cyclic block, and choose an eigenvector. A nonzero stalk component of that eigenvector has the same eigenvalue after taking the e-th power, so μ^e is an eigenvalue of F_x. Since the residue-field extension has degree e, q_x=q_y^e. If G has all local eigenvalues of weight at most w, then |ι(μ)|^e=|ι(μ^e)|≤q_x^{w/2}=q_y^{ew/2}; taking the nonnegative e-th root gives |ι(μ)|≤q_y^{w/2}. If G is punctually ι-pure of weight w, the inequality is an equality throughout and gives |ι(μ)|=q_y^{w/2}.

source.place: Displayed absolute-value calculation; elementary eigenvector argument on cyclic blocks

proof.text: The argument applies to every closed y and every eigenvalue μ of the direct-image local Frobenius. By the definitions in [def-weil-punctual-weights], these inequalities are exactly the punctual upper-weight assertion, and the equalities are exactly punctual ι-purity of weight w. If a fibre or stalk is zero there are no eigenvalues and the assertion is vacuous.
